issues.description: The solution uses the identifier 'lecturer' for the Course property and initializer parameter, while the problem statement and the template use 'instructor'. Furthermore, the solution's Client and Developer code call Course with an 'instructor' label and access course.instructor, which does not exist in the solution Course implementation. This naming mismatch is likely an unintentional oversight and will cause compile errors and confusion when students compare the template/problem to the solution or run the provided Client code.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the identifier for the Course instructor consistent across all artifacts. The simplest fix is to rename the solution's Course property and initializer parameter from 'lecturer' to 'instructor' and update any internal uses (initializer, property, and any references in Client.swift and Developer.swift) to 'instructor' so they match the problem statement and template. Alternatively, update the problem statement and template to use 'lecturer', but keeping 'instructor' is recommended to avoid breaking the Client and Developer code.
